name: PayJunction

google.heading: PayJunction on Google
google.summary: 29 reviews on the Santa Barbara listing, 4.6 average, 26 of them five star. A small record, and most of it is four to six years old, so read it as a set of accounts from the late 2010s rather than as a current rating. What those accounts have in common is worth something: they are from finance and operations people rather than founders, and they credit two specific things. Recurring payments handled well enough that a veterinary practice brought its wellness plan billing in house, and support that a controller running eight car dealerships and two body shops describes as reliable across account changes and limit increases. The three one-star reviews are about the card terminals, which reviewers found badly designed, and one about funds being held. Nobody has reviewed it recently either way.

themes.label: Recurring billing that let firms bring plans in house
themes.detail: A veterinary practice describes moving wellness plan payments off a third party because PayJunction's recurring feature handled it.

themes.label: Support that holds up across many accounts
themes.detail: A controller running ten businesses describes consistent help with account changes, limit increases and navigation.

themes.label: The terminals
themes.detail: The sharpest negative is about the card readers being poorly designed, from someone who says every business they visit dislikes them.

themes.label: The record is old
themes.detail: Most of these reviews are four to six years old. A 4.6 from 29 reviews of that vintage is a historical impression, not a current one.

quotes.text: Excellent customer service. PayJunction has always exceeded our expectations when we need help. The recurring payments feature they offer allowed us to bring our wellness plan payment processing in house.
Worst designed credit card machines known to man. Every business I have been to with there readers hates them.

noRedditReason: PayJunction has essentially no Reddit presence. The only thread that asks about it is from January 2018, posted by someone considering a sales job there rather than by a merchant, and it drew three replies. There is nothing to summarise without inventing it.
